solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: An eccentric leading investigator may

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ... is an informal name for a crazy or unpredictable person
second meaning: read as a verb phrase, a lead detective may head a case, that is be in charge of the inquiry

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a cryptic reading: split the answer into two words and it becomes what a chief detective does, head (lead) a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A head case is British slang for someone wildly unpredictable or mad, an informal synonym for an oddball.

clue.text: Give out some cards

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... something over is to give it
second meaning: the set of cards a player is dealt in a game

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a dealer's instruction; the two meanings are a verb (pass over) and a noun (a player's cards).
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means pass or present to someone; as a noun it is the group of cards held by one player.

clue.text: Vault leaving sprinter's bottom in endless pain

indicators.note: the shortened pain word holds the sprinter's last letter inside it
the word for pain loses its final letter, its end

parts.note: an ache is a dull persistent pain

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its last letter, here the end of sprinter

parts.note: the last letter of the word sprinter

explanation.surface: A pole-vaulter quits the event with an aching backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vault' looks like the athletic event, but it is the architectural sense: a curved roof or arch.
explanation.definitionFit: A vault is an arched roof, and an arch is the curved structure that forms it, so the two are near synonyms.

clue.text: Old Lancashire factory's motto: nil carborundum legitimi — initially mistaken!

indicators.note: a mistaken version of the words gets them wrong, so their letters are put into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letters of carborundum and legitimi are used

parts.note: the first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A mill-owner's mock-Latin slogan, 'don't let the bastards grind you down', is admitted to be bad Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nil carborundum illegitimi' is a mock-Latin joke motto; the clue garbles it, and that garbling is the hint to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancashire's nineteenth-century economy rested on factories that spun and wove raw cotton, the classic mill of the industrial north.

clue.text: Drawing of small boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A picture of a little sailing vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough, quick drawing, so the noun is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Feature of Asian country left incomplete

indicators.note: the country's name is left without its final letter, so it is incomplete

parts.note: China is the large country in East Asia

explanation.surface: Something characteristic of an Asian nation was never finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' seems to mean a characteristic of the country, but it is a facial feature.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is a part of the face, and parts of the face are called features.

clue.text: Present non-voluntary movements for nonconformists

parts.note: here means present, in attendance
tics are involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: Showing involuntary twitches as a mark of dissent.
explanation.definitionFit: Heretics hold opinions at odds with accepted religious doctrine, so they refuse to conform.

clue.text: Snort is likely at first to come out of them?

definitions.text: Snort is likely at first to come out of them?

indicators.note: letters that come out differently are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: only the opening letter of likely is used

parts.note: the opening letter of the word likely

explanation.surface: A snort is most likely to emerge from the nose's openings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a snort does come out of these.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostrils are the two openings of the nose, which is where a snort of breath is expelled.

clue.text: Drink before matches in formal men's attire

parts.note: to neck a drink is British slang for gulping it down
ties are sporting matches, especially cup ties in football

explanation.surface: A drink before the game, in a suit and tie.
explanation.walkthrough: To neck is British slang for drinking quickly; a cup tie is a knockout football match.
explanation.definitionFit: Neckties are the strips of cloth worn knotted at the collar as part of formal male dress.

clue.text: Weapons, as intercepted by Royal Marines

indicators.note: the word as is intercepted, cut through the middle, by the marines' two letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A shipment of guns is seized by a commando unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms is the general word for guns and other weaponry.

clue.text: Compare group once more on street

parts.note: a set is a group of things that belong together
again means once more

explanation.surface: Weighing a gang up against another one down the road.
explanation.definitionFit: To set one thing against another is to weigh them side by side, a phrasal synonym for compare.

clue.text: Hotel that's altered the records

indicators.note: the letters of the words are altered, changed into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hotel has been fiddling its books.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dorchester is a famous luxury hotel on Park Lane in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorchester is a specific grand hotel in Mayfair, so it is an example of a hotel.

clue.text: Hide from animal left with a doctor's family

parts.note: taken as written
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree, and the 's adds S
kin are your relatives

explanation.surface: Someone leaves with a doctor's relatives, trying to hide from a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambskin is the skin of a young sheep, a hide taken from that particular animal.

clue.text: Most calm and yet is French!

parts.note: still and yet both mean nevertheless
est is the French for is

explanation.surface: Calm and yet French: a cool continental temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: Still means calm and unmoving, so the superlative is the calmest of all.

clue.text: Faculty US monk regularly visited in season

indicators.note: the phrase is visited at regular intervals, every other letter starting with the second

parts.note: the even-placed letters of these three words, read in order

explanation.surface: An American monk calls round at a college department at a certain time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: Autumn is the season between summer and winter, called fall in American English.

clue.text: Package Norm left outside church

indicators.note: the norm and left letters sit outside the church abbreviation, around it

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf

explanation.surface: Someone called Norm leaves a package at a church door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Norm' looks like a man's name, but it is the noun norm, a standard; CE is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped package sent through the post.

clue.text: Henry dropping in altitude, with seven in front?

indicators.note: H for henry, the unit of inductance, drops from the top of the word to the bottom in this down clue

parts.note: height is altitude

explanation.surface: A king called Henry losing height, with seven others ahead of him in line.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a king (the eighth, aptly); here it is H, the physics unit, moved from top to bottom of the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth item in a sequence has exactly seven others ahead of it.

clue.text: "Labials": aka unusual things for musicians

indicators.note: the letters are arranged in an unusual way, a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Lip sounds, otherwise known as odd things for musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Balalaikas are triangular Russian stringed instruments, items that musicians play.

clue.text: Singer turning up in Scotland

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
the letters sit inside the word Scotland

parts.note: the four letters in the middle of Scotland, after its first two

explanation.surface: A vocalist appears in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An alto is a singer with a low female or high male voice.

clue.text: One's twice becoming a goddess

indicators.note: twice means the letters are written two times in a row

parts.note: one's is read as I'S, I for one plus S, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone is doubly transformed into a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'One's' as the Roman numeral for one followed by the S of the contraction, then write that 'twice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Isis was the Egyptian mother goddess, wife of Osiris.

clue.text: Bender one proposes to go on?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the joint that bends the leg
second meaning: a man proposing marriage traditionally goes down on one ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bender' suggests a drinking spree; here it is simply something that bends.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint of the leg, and a suitor kneels on it when asking for marriage.

clue.text: Painful condition: one's going round hospital

indicators.note: the ones word goes round the hospital letter, enclosing it

parts.note: singles are ones, single units; read the apostrophe as a plural

explanation.surface: An ailment is doing the rounds of the hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Shingles is a painful viral rash caused by the chickenpox virus reawakening along a nerve.

clue.text: A, B, C, D, F or G?

definitions.meaning: on the surface a list of letters, or a set of grades
each is a musical pitch name, and E is the one missing from the list

explanation.walkthrough: Each listed letter names a musical note; the trick is that E is left out, so the answer splits as NOT E.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical pitches are named with the letters A to G, so each of these letters is one of them.

clue.text: Travels around the ramshackle end of district — to see these?

definitions.text: Travels around the ramshackle end of district — to see these?

indicators.note: the travels word goes around the other letters

parts.note: goes means travels

indicators.note: something ramshackle is tumbledown, so the letters of the are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only the final letter of district is used

parts.note: the last letter of the word district

explanation.surface: A tourist heads for the run-down side of town to look at its slums.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: these are what you would see on a trip to a city's run-down quarter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghettoes are poor, crowded urban quarters where a minority group is concentrated.
